name: comp-46

frames.best_why: The US flag has appeared in the country selector and the number is fully formatted, showing the whole idea.

tagline: A phone field that spots the country and adds its flag as you type.
summary: A labelled phone field joined to a country selector. Typing an international number spaces the digits into a readable phone number and makes the selector detect the country and show its flag.
appearance: A label sits above a joined control on black: a country selector holding a small handset icon and a chevron, then a long rounded input. Once a code is typed a US flag replaces the handset, and the digits run across in spaced groups.
behaviour: Typing formats the number with spaces and the selector watches the country code, swapping in the matching flag. The clip enters +1 415 555 0132, the flag changes to the United States and the caret stays in the field.
demo_content: Label Phone number, placeholder Enter phone number, typed +1 415 555 0132, plus a library credit line.
search_phrases: country picker next to a number
type a number and space it
flag appears when typing a number
use_when: Sign-up or contact forms that accept phone numbers from more than one country.
avoid_when: It ships a visible third-party credit link and pulls in a sizeable phone-number library.
customise: The label and placeholder are fixed in the file and the country list comes from the phone library; field and selector styling are classes there.
weight_why: Phone metadata plus parsing on each keystroke is heavier than a plain text field.

a11y.note: The label and country select are named properly, but a country detected from typing is not announced to screen readers.

issues: A visible react-phone-number-input credit line ships under the field.
polish_why: Tidy joined field with a nice flag reveal, though the credit line and plain styling hold it back.
